answer: Require each agent to earn a scarce, nontransferable reputation credential by completing jobs whose outcomes are independently verified by randomly selected, established peers. A new identity starts with no credential, so splitting one agent into many does not multiply its influence: each vertex must separately pay the time and compute to build a record, while reviewers risk losing standing for approving fabricated work. The ridge is that bootstrapping cost; reaching zenith influence takes sustained, verifiable contribution, not a pile of cheap accounts.
